name: Troy Edward Wilson
current_role: Co-founder, Chairman, President & CEO, Kura Oncology (NASDAQ: KURA)
profile: Biotech serial founder with a Berkeley PhD in bioorganic chemistry and an NYU law degree. Co-founded Intellikine (sold to Takeda), Ambrx (sold to J&J), Araxes/Wellspring (KRAS inhibitors), Avidity Biosciences (CEO to 2019, chair until Novartis deal) and Kura Oncology, which he has led since 2014.
interesting_fact: His Araxes Pharma/Wellspring Biosciences teams were early pioneers of small-molecule inhibitors of KRAS, long considered an 'undruggable' cancer target.
deep_cut_fact: He was named a Hertz Fellow in 1990, the highly selective Hertz Foundation graduate fellowship in applied science, before earning his Berkeley PhD.
notes: Also on boards of Puma Biotechnology, Atrium Therapeutics, Cartography, Montara, Cipher Genetics. Best route is Kura media/IR.

name: Matthew K Schatzman
profile: LNG executive with nearly four decades in energy. Former EVP of Global Energy Marketing & Shipping at BG Group and senior executive at Dynegy. Joined NextDecade in 2017, CEO since 2018 and Chairman since 2019, he led the financing and construction of the Rio Grande LNG export terminal in Brownsville, Texas.
interesting_fact: Under him NextDecade financed the multi-train Rio Grande LNG project (about 30 MTPA initially, site permitted/planned for up to ~60 MTPA with ten trains), one of the largest US LNG export developments.
deep_cut_fact: He began his energy career at Transco Pipeline, a Williams subsidiary, and holds a BA in political science from Yale; he also sits on the National Petroleum Council.
notes: Strong fit for an energy podcast (US LNG exports). Appears linked to Baker Hughes annual meeting materials (possible board nominee) - not verified. Route via NextDecade media contact.

name: Todd M Duchene
current_role: EVP, Chief Legal & Administrative Officer, Chief Compliance Officer and Secretary, Core Scientific (NASDAQ: CORZ)
profile: Veteran corporate general counsel who joined bitcoin miner turned AI/HPC data-center operator Core Scientific in 2019, steering it through its 2022-24 Chapter 11 restructuring and its pivot to hosting AI compute (e.g., CoreWeave). Previously GC at FLIR Systems, Nuance Communications, National Semiconductor, Solectron, Fisher Scientific and OfficeMax.
interesting_fact: He briefly served as Core Scientific's President (Nov 2022-May 2023) during its bankruptcy, before returning to the chief legal/administrative role as the company re-emerged and pivoted to AI data centers.
deep_cut_fact: Before data centers he was general counsel of thermal-imaging maker FLIR Systems (2014-2019); he was named to the Legal 500 GC Powerlist Texas 2025 (Information Technology).
notes: Lawyer/executive rather than founder; low public profile. Relevant to data-center theme. Career history partly from aggregator profiles (theorg, insidertrades).

name: Michael P Donaldson
current_role: EVP & Chief Legal Officer (also Corporate Secretary), EOG Resources (NYSE: EOG)
profile: Houston energy lawyer who has spent his career in-house in oil and gas (Pennzoil, Union Texas Petroleum, Burlington Resources, TODCO) after starting as a commercial trial lawyer and at Akin Gump. Joined EOG in 2007, became general counsel, and was elevated to Chief Legal Officer in 2025, overseeing legal, government relations, internal audit and land administration.
interesting_fact: As EOG's top lawyer he leads not only the legal department but also government relations, internal audit and land administration for one of the largest US shale producers.
deep_cut_fact: As a South Texas College of Law student he worked as a courtroom usher at the landmark Pennzoil v. Texaco appeal held on campus (Joe Jamail's case) - and later went in-house at Pennzoil. He now chairs the school's board of visitors.
notes: Low public profile corporate lawyer; first-generation lawyer, Miami University (Ohio) undergrad, STCL '87, UH LLM. Best route: EOG media office or via South Texas College of Law.

name: Jamie S Gorelick
current_role: Senior Counsel, WilmerHale; Lead Independent Director of Amazon; director of Verisign
profile: Brooklyn-born Harvard-trained lawyer who was General Counsel of the Department of Defense and then one of the longest-serving US Deputy Attorneys General (1994-97), later a 9/11 Commissioner. At WilmerHale since 2003 (chaired its Regulatory & Government Affairs dept 2015-2025); her SEC-reported wealth comes largely from Amazon board service since 2012.
interesting_fact: She is Amazon's Lead Independent Director and has served on Amazon's board since February 2012; she also chairs Verisign's governance and nominating committee.
deep_cut_fact: Early in her career she held senior roles at the US Department of Energy, and she co-authored the treatise 'Destruction of Evidence' (Wiley, 1983); she also once sat on the board of oilfield-services giant Schlumberger.
notes: Professional email is published on her WilmerHale bio. Prominent DC figure; energy/crisis angle (represented BP after Deepwater Horizon, advised Norfolk Southern). Some politically contested history (9/11 'wall' memo, Fannie Mae) - avoid in outreach.

name: Gregory L Gibson
current_role: Director, First Financial Corporation (Terre Haute, IN; NASDAQ: THFF); President, ReTec Corporation
profile: Terre Haute, Indiana entrepreneur and developer, president of waste-management consulting firm ReTec Corporation and involved in several other ventures. A director of First Financial Corporation since 1994 (renominated in 2026 for a term to 2029) and a Rose-Hulman Institute of Technology trustee and alumnus.
interesting_fact: He has served on state bodies including the Indiana Judicial Nominating Commission, the Ports of Indiana Commission and the Indiana Utility Regulatory Nominating Commission.
deep_cut_fact: An engineering-school graduate (B.S., Rose-Hulman Institute of Technology), he now sits on its board of trustees and chairs the boards of Hospice of the Wabash Valley, the Visiting Nurses Association and the Terre Haute Convention and Visitors Bureau.
notes: Private regional businessman; no personal published contact found (web search budget exhausted mid-lane). Possible route via First Financial Corp corporate secretary per proxy, or Terre Haute CVB. Also known locally as a Terre Haute developer/casino investor - verify before outreach.

name: Geoffrey Gates Scott
current_role: Independent Director (Chair, Corporate Governance & Nominating Committee), Aehr Test Systems (NASDAQ: AEHR); private investor
profile: Retired investment manager who ran Scott Asset Management (1995-2017), a small-cap focused investment group, after careers at Merrill Lynch's Capital Markets Group (1991-95) and Chase Manhattan's Corporate Banking Group (1973-90). A Dartmouth graduate, he has been on the board of semiconductor test-equipment maker Aehr Test Systems since 2020.
interesting_fact: Aehr Test Systems, where he chairs the governance committee, makes wafer-level burn-in and test systems used for silicon-carbide power chips and, increasingly, AI processors.
deep_cut_fact: He spent 17 years (1973-1990) in Chase Manhattan's Corporate Banking Group before moving to Merrill Lynch and later founding his own small-cap investment firm.

public_contacts.value: PondelWilkinson (Aehr IR): Laurie Berman lberman@pondel.com; tkehrli@pondel.com

notes: Very low public profile private investor, age ~77. Only route found is via Aehr's IR agency or c/o Aehr Test Systems, Fremont CA.

name: Dana Aftab
current_role: Executive Vice President, Research and Development, Exelixis, Inc. (NASDAQ: EXEL)
profile: Pharmacologist (UCSB BA, Yale PhD, Berkeley postdoc) who joined Exelixis' drug discovery group in 1998 and led teams behind its approved medicines, including the cancer drug cabozantinib (Cabometyx/Cometriq). He later ran translational research, business operations and research as CSO, and since August 2025 heads all of Exelixis' R&D.
interesting_fact: He has been at Exelixis for nearly three decades and was part of the discovery teams for cabozantinib, now a multi-billion-dollar oncology franchise for the company.
deep_cut_fact: As EVP of Business Operations (2016-2022) the scientist oversaw Exelixis' corporate site development, including opening new laboratory buildings on its Alameda campus; his Berkeley postdoc was in oncogene signaling.

public_contacts.value: shubbard@exelixis.com (Susan Hubbard, EVP Public Affairs & Investor Relations)

notes: Scientist-executive, low public profile. Best route via Exelixis public affairs/IR.

name: Zhu Guang
current_role: CEO, Du Xiaoman Financial (as of its 2018 spin-off from Baidu; current 2026 status not verified)
profile: Chinese internet executive (朱光) who was Baidu Senior Vice President and General Manager of its Financial Services Group. When Baidu divested a majority stake in the unit to investors led by TPG and Carlyle in 2018 (raising ~US$1.9bn), it was renamed Du Xiaoman Financial and he became its CEO, leading the AI-driven consumer-credit and wealth-management fintech.
interesting_fact: Du Xiaoman grew out of Baidu's financial services unit founded in December 2015; at the 2018 spin-off Baidu kept about 42% and Zhu said it would use Baidu AI to deliver 'technology-driven, trustworthy financial services'.
notes: Hurun lists him as a 'founder' but he was the Baidu executive who led the spin-off rather than a classic founder. Could not verify his 2026 role or find a published Du Xiaoman press contact (web search budget exhausted; Wikipedia rate-limited). Approach via Du Xiaoman corporate communications.

name: David Wiesen
profile: One of four co-founders of neighborhood social network Nextdoor in 2008, alongside Nirav Tolia, Sarah Leary and Prakash Janakiraman. Nextdoor launched nationally in the US in October 2011, was backed early by Benchmark and Shasta Ventures, and went public via SPAC in 2021 (NYSE: KIND); Wiesen keeps a very low public profile.
interesting_fact: Nextdoor, which he co-founded, was originally piloted as a private network for neighborhoods and launched nationally in October 2011 with Benchmark Capital as an early investor.
notes: Very little public information; current activities unverified (web search budget exhausted, no SEC filings under his name). Route via Nextdoor press office or his co-founders.

name: Gabriel Flateman
current_role: Co-founder of Casper Sleep; listed as executive officer/director of Yaysay, Inc. in a 2023 SEC Form D (connection not independently confirmed)
profile: 'Gabe' Flateman is one of the five co-founders of direct-to-consumer mattress brand Casper (2014, with Philip Krim, Neil Parikh, Luke Sherwin and Jeff Chapin), reportedly its technology lead. Casper launched April 22, 2014, IPO'd on the NYSE in 2020, was taken private in 2022 and sold to Carpenter Co. in 2024.
interesting_fact: Casper launched on April 22, 2014 after a $1.85M seed round and became one of the defining 'bed-in-a-box' DTC startups, reaching unicorn status before its 2020 IPO.
notes: Low public profile. A Greenwich, CT-based Gabriel Flateman filed a Form D as officer of startup Yaysay, Inc. in Oct 2023 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1996695/000199669523000001/primary_doc.xml) - likely but not confirmed to be him. Web search budget exhausted before deeper checks.

name: Gil Shoham
profile: Listed by Hurun as a founder of Israeli adtech/app-monetization company ironSource (founded 2010 in Tel Aviv; merged into Unity Technologies in a ~$4.4B all-stock deal completed November 2022). I could not confirm his role at ironSource or his current activities from accessible sources.
interesting_fact: ironSource, founded in Tel Aviv in 2010, went public via SPAC in 2021 and was absorbed by Unity in November 2022, with former ironSource holders owning ~26.5% of the combined company.
notes: Identity not confirmed: Wikipedia names only Tomer Bar-Zeev among ironSource's four founders; no SEC filing mentions 'Gil Shoham' (a different person, Tal Shoham, ex-ironSource, sits on GDEV's board - do not confuse). Web search budget exhausted; needs manual follow-up.

name: Brian Lee
current_role: Co-Founder & Managing Director, BAM Ventures (Los Angeles); co-founder, Arena Club
profile: Seoul-born, UCLA-educated former Skadden lawyer turned serial consumer-internet founder: co-founded LegalZoom (2001, with Robert Shapiro), ShoeDazzle (2009, with Kim Kardashian) and The Honest Company (with Jessica Alba; CEO until 2017; IPO 2021). Since 2017 he runs LA venture firm BAM Ventures and in 2022 co-founded sports-card platform Arena Club with Derek Jeter.
interesting_fact: He has co-founded companies with three different celebrity partners - attorney Robert Shapiro (LegalZoom), Kim Kardashian (ShoeDazzle) and Jessica Alba (The Honest Company) - and later Derek Jeter (Arena Club).
deep_cut_fact: He graduated magna cum laude in economics/business from UCLA and practiced law at Skadden, Arps before co-founding LegalZoom in 2001; Forbes named him one of the 25 most notable Korean-American entrepreneurs in 2009.
notes: Common name - make sure outreach targets BAM Ventures' Brian Lee. Active LA VC; BAM site lists Facebook/Twitter/Instagram links but they appear to be the firm's, not personal.

name: Eytan Elbaz
current_role: Co-founder, Scopely (current executive/board role not verified)
profile: Los Angeles tech entrepreneur who co-founded Applied Semantics (acquired by Google in April 2003) and then, in 2011, mobile-games company Scopely with Walter Driver, Ankur Bulsara and Eric Futoran. Scopely (Monopoly Go!, Star Trek Fleet Command, Stumble Guys) was bought by Saudi-backed Savvy Games Group for $4.9B in 2023 and in 2025 acquired Niantic's games business including Pokemon GO for ~$3.5B.
interesting_fact: Scopely, which he co-founded in LA in 2011, now owns Pokemon GO after buying Niantic's games business in a ~$3.5B deal completed May 2025.
deep_cut_fact: Before Scopely he co-founded Applied Semantics; the 'AdSense' name originally belonged to Applied Semantics and Google adopted it after acquiring the company in April 2003.
notes: Low-profile co-founder; podcast angle = two big exits (Google AdSense lineage, Savvy $4.9B). Current role unverified (web search budget exhausted).

name: Jack Zubarev
profile: Ilya 'Jack' Zubarev is one of the three co-founders of Swiss-headquartered (Schaffhausen) cyber-protection and backup company Acronis, founded in 2003 with Serg Bell and Stanislav Protassov as a spin-off of SWsoft (later Parallels/Virtuozzo). Acronis reached a multibillion-dollar valuation; it is now run by professional CEOs (Prakash Panjwani from Oct 2026).
interesting_fact: Acronis began in 2003 as a spin-off of server-virtualization firm SWsoft, the company that later became Parallels and Virtuozzo.
notes: Very low public profile; Wikipedia lists him as Ilya Zubarev. Could not verify current activities (web search budget exhausted). Route via Acronis PR.

name: Nissim Tapiro
current_role: Co-founder, NEXT Insurance (now ERGO NEXT Insurance); current title not verified
profile: Israeli tech entrepreneur who co-founded NEXT Insurance in 2016 with Guy Goldstein and Alon Huri to sell fast, tailored, digital small-business insurance. NEXT grew to cover 750,000+ US small businesses across 1,300+ professions and in 2025 was acquired by Munich Re's ERGO Group, becoming ERGO NEXT Insurance.
interesting_fact: The founders started NEXT after experiencing first-hand how slow and confusing buying small-business insurance was; the company now insures more than 750,000 US small businesses.
notes: Low public profile (typically the technology-side co-founder). Founders are widely reported to have previously built mobile bill-pay app Check (sold to Intuit 2014), but I could not confirm Tapiro's role from an accessible source. No published press email found.

name: Thomas Pischke
current_role: Co-founder and Managing Director (Geschaeftsfuehrer), Trade Republic Bank GmbH, Berlin
profile: Physicist who co-founded Trade Republic in Munich in 2015 (originally 'Neon Trading', inside Comdirect's startup incubator) with Christian Hecker and Marco Cancellieri. The Berlin-based neobroker/bank brought commission-light mobile investing to millions of Europeans; it raised $900M at a $5B valuation in 2021 and a December 2025 secondary valued it at EUR 12.5B. He remains one of its managing directors.
interesting_fact: Trade Republic began in 2015 under the name Neon Trading inside Comdirect Bank's startup incubator before becoming one of Europe's most valuable fintechs (EUR 12.5B in Dec 2025).
deep_cut_fact: The three founders came from deliberately different disciplines: Pischke is a physicist, Christian Hecker a philosopher and Marco Cancellieri a computer scientist.
notes: Low-profile co-founder (Hecker is the public face). Trade Republic site has a Press section but I could not retrieve a published press email.

name: Florian Otto
current_role: Co-founder & Chief Executive Officer, Cedar (New York healthcare payments)
profile: Co-founder and CEO of Cedar, a New York-based healthcare financial-experience platform that helps hospitals and physician groups handle patient billing, payments and financial assistance. Cedar has processed over $13.6B in payments for 63M+ patients and in 2025-26 has pushed into agentic AI for patient billing (Kora platform, Cedar Cover for Medicaid/affordability).
interesting_fact: Cedar says its AI is powered by more than 1.5 billion patient interactions and has processed over $13.6 billion in patient payments.
notes: AI/healthcare-fintech angle. Background before Cedar not verified (web search budget exhausted).

name: Luiz Calicchio
current_role: Listed by Hurun as a founder of C6 Bank (current role not verified)
profile: Named by Hurun among the founders of C6 Bank, the Sao Paulo digital bank started in 2018 (public launch August 2019) by former BTG Pactual executive Marcelo Kalim and a group of Brazilian finance and technology executives. JPMorgan Chase bought 40% of C6 in 2021 and raised its stake to 46% in 2023. I could not confirm Calicchio's specific role from accessible sources.
interesting_fact: JPMorgan Chase's 2021 investment in C6 Bank (40%, raised to 46% in 2023) was its big bet on Brazilian retail digital banking.
notes: Not mentioned on C6 Bank's Wikipedia pages; C6 site blocked automated access; no SEC mentions. Web search budget exhausted - needs manual verification before outreach.

name: Mariano Suarez-Battan
current_role: Co-founder and Executive Chairman, Mural (as of July 2024)
profile: Argentine entrepreneur ('Mariano Battan') who co-founded Mural, the visual-collaboration/digital-whiteboard software company that boomed during the shift to remote work and reached unicorn status. He led Mural as CEO through its growth years, handed the CEO role to outside executives (David Baga in 2022, then Leigh-Margaret Stull in July 2024) and serves as Executive Chairman.
interesting_fact: Mural became one of the leading 'digital whiteboard' platforms for remote and hybrid teams, with a Microsoft partnership and a $1B+ valuation per Hurun.
notes: Goes by 'Mariano Battan' in Mural materials. Earlier career (reportedly a gaming-studio founder in Buenos Aires) not verified - web search budget exhausted.
